name: Smt. S. Phangnon Konyak
education: M.A. (English Literature) Educated at University of Delhi
present_address: Bunglow No.14-A, Ferozshah Road, New Delhi 110001
social_activities: Chief Functionary, Walo Organisation, Mon, District, 2005 - 2020; implemented the TI (Targeted Intervention) project at Aboi for injecting drug users and other vulnerable population; also implemented ‘Link Workers Scheme’ in Mon district for the prevention of HIV/AIDS; as Member of the Scientific Advisory Committee, assisted KVK Mon in their activity,in Mon District; successfully implemented AIS (Alternative Innovative Schooling) SSA in admitting 1650 dropout/never enrolled children aged 6-14 years into formal schooling in Mon EBRC and Aboi EBRC covering 37 villages; initiated opening of libraries for children in all the villages of Mon District with the support of PRATHAM and conducted ASER survey in the district; initiated the process of documenting Konyak Cultural heritage, with active support of CCK, Ambedkar University, Delhi and Anthropological Society of India in Mon District; selected as Member of State Level Selection Committee for Juvenile Justice Board and Child Welfare Committee, Nagaland, 2018; President, (i) Eastern Nagaland Women Organisation, Kohima Unit, 2019-2020 and (ii) SPOAA, a society registered under the aegis of ENWO, ENPO, ENSF, the three apex community organizations of eastern Nagaland
other_information: Vice-President, Tuensang Mon Students’ Union, Delhi, 2002-2003; Women Coordinator, Konyak Students’ Union, 2006-09; Member, Board of Directors, Nagaland State Co-operative Bank, 2008-10; Advisor, Konyak Students’ Union, 2009-11; Member, Consortia Advisory Committee for NAIP, ICAR (Northeast) from Nagaland, 2009-14; Vice-President, Konyak Nyupuh Sheko Khong, 2012-14; Member, Child Welfare Committee, Mon District, 2013-15; Council Member, Sustainable Development Forum of Nagaland since 2016; joined B.J.P. in 2017; served as State General Secretary, B.J.P. Mahila Morcha, Nagaland Unit; State President, B.J.P. Mahila Morcha, Nagaland since 2020
